whatItSays.everyKeyIsOneParcelWrittenOnce: distinctGeometries === 1 on every one of the 82
whatItSays.tileDuplication: each key's rows carry the SAME feature_index and the same bbox -- one source polygon written once per 0.02-degree tile its bbox straddles (R006142: 2 rows, feature_index 185424 on both, tiles g0.02:-97.40000,30.56000 and g0.02:-97.38000,30.56000)
whatItSays.noPublishedIdentifierReachesThem: reachedByPublishedPair false on all 82, and none is carried by the situs fallback -- which is why cadPresent could not accept them
whatItSays.theRollDoesNameThem: inCountyRollByPropId true on all 82: the county's declared roll holds a row under the node's own R key. The fill's CAD leg deliberately cannot see it for 48491 (P-335's published-pair rule), which is what left the account leg silent on exactly these keys
whatItSays.theyAreInThePublishedIndex: inPublishedIndex true on all 82, so the county itself publishes them as parcel ids
whatItSays.theThreeDissenters: R674569/R674570/R674571 are the only 3 with no owner and no situs on their rows, i.e. the situs-agreement derivation would have refused them; the keyspace derivation accepts them

controls.phantomNote: PRIVATE ROAD: rows 2, distinct_geometries 1 -- the SAME shape as all 82, so no geometry measurement can separate it; and cad_property holds NO row for it (0). The separation is the KEY: it is `other`-shaped in a county whose roll files R<digits> and digits.
controls.prOperaFalsifier: the pre-change predicate (count(*) = 1) refuses all 82 and refuses PRIVATE ROAD -- so it never separated the two populations, it refused 82 real parcels to catch one label key by luck
